Teach your OpenClaw to solve Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equations with deep learning
github:https://github.com/Reedcgx/Deep-HJB-Solver-Skill

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: deep-hjb-solver-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides a legitimate framework for solving Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations using the Deep Galerkin Method (DGM) in TensorFlow. The included Python files (assets/src/, scripts/scaffold_hjb_problem.py) and documentation (SKILL.md, references/) are consistent with scientific computing and machine learning workflows. While SKILL.md contains directives for the AI agent to execute shell commands (mkdir, cp) without user confirmation to set up the workspace, these actions are restricted to local file management of bundled assets and do not exhibit signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized remote access.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a legit HJB scaffolding framework and bundles the expected code, but its runtime instructions tell the agent to copy files into the user's repository immediately and without asking, and there are small inconsistencies about how that copy should be done — this behavior is disproportionate and worth caution before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the included assets and scripts: the skill bundles a TensorFlow DGM framework, scaffolding script, plotting utilities, and templates needed to create new HJB problems. There are no unrelated required env vars or external services. Requesting to copy the bundled framework into a target repo is coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to run shell copy (cp) commands immediately 'without asking the user for permission or confirmation' and to proceed only after they complete. That grants the agent broad unilateral ability to modify files in the user's working directory. Additionally, SKILL.md's raw cp commands can overwrite existing files, whereas the included Python scaffold script (scripts/scaffold_hjb_problem.py) implements safer checks (it skips copying if src/ already exists). This mismatch and the 'do not ask' language are scope creep and present an unnecessary risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install/download step; the skill is instruction-only and bundles all source in assets/. No network downloads or opaque installers are used. The only file operations are local copies from the bundled assets, which is proportionate to scaffolding a code template.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, binaries, or credentials. The only runtime expectation is standard Python/TensorFlow tooling (requirements.txt lists tensorflow, numpy, matplotlib), which is consistent with the purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or other elevated platform privileges. However, the SKILL.md instructs the agent to write a copy of the framework into the target repository immediately; while this is not a persistent platform-level privilege, it is an intrusive filesystem action and should not be executed without explicit user approval.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill bundles a legitimate TensorFlow DGM scaffold and templates (no network calls or hidden endpoints), but its runtime instructions tell the agent to copy files into your repository immediately and explicitly say not to ask for permission. Before installing or running: 1) Do NOT let an agent run the raw cp commands unless you explicitly approve them. 2) Prefer running the provided Python scaffold script (scripts/scaffold_hjb_problem.py) yourself — it includes checks and will avoid copying if src/ already exists. 3) Back up your repo or run the scaffold in an isolated directory to avoid accidental overwrites. 4) Inspect the bundled files (assets/src/, plot_training_csv.py, requirements.txt) to ensure they meet your needs. 5) Be aware that installing the listed requirements (tensorflow>=2.15.0) may be large and require GPU/OS compatibility. If you want the agent to perform changes, require it to ask for explicit, per-action confirmation and to show diffs before writing files.
